title: Satellites Now Use AI to Catch Wildfires the Size of a Tennis Court
hook: Three new satellites just launched with one job: spot a wildfire early enough to matter — using AI that checks every image against a thousand before it, to tell smoke from a false alarm.
key_points: FireSat's first three operational satellites launched July 7, 2026 from Vandenberg Space Force Base.
Built by Google Research, the nonprofit Earth Fire Alliance, and satellite maker Muon Space.
Sensors can spot fires as small as 5x5 meters — much earlier than most existing satellites.
AI compares each new image against roughly 1,000 past images of the same spot to confirm a real fire.
Goal: cover every fire-prone region twice a day now, hourly by 2029, every 20 minutes by the early 2030s.
content_html: Three new satellites launched from California on July 7, 2026 with a specific mission: catch wildfires while they're still small enough to stop. The FireSat program — a partnership between Google Research, the nonprofit Earth Fire Alliance, and satellite maker Muon Space — reports its sensors can spot a fire as small as 5x5 meters, far earlier than most wildfire-watching satellites manage today.
extra_html: The hard part isn't just seeing a hot spot — it's telling a real, growing fire from sunlight glinting off a rooftop or a routine controlled burn. That's where the AI comes in: each new image gets compared against roughly a thousand past images of that same patch of ground, plus local weather conditions, before the system flags it as a genuine wildfire. For now, the three satellites give fire agencies a look at any fire-prone region on Earth about twice a day. As more launch, FireSat aims for hourly updates by 2029 and a refresh every 20 minutes — once more than 50 satellites are in orbit — by the early 2030s. It's a useful reminder that not all consequential AI is a chatbot: some of it is quietly watching the planet from orbit.

related.title: AI in Everyday Tools
related.hook: You've used AI for years without calling it that — every time your phone unlocks with your face, your maps reroute around traffic, or your inbox filters spam.

related.title: How AI Learns
related.hook: Training an AI is like teaching by flashcards on a massive scale: show it an example, let it guess, tell it how wrong it was, and nudge it to do better — billions of times.
